_about: Word traps (/knowledge/false-friends): English words that learners mix up – look-alikes (kitchen/chicken, receipt/recipe) and false friends from other languages (become ≠ German bekommen, actual ≠ aktuell/actual, embarrassed ≠ Spanish embarazada) – each with the funny wrong sentence, the right one and a memory trick. *word* marks the word to highlight. quiz.a is the right option. Emoji are OpenMoji SVGs already in public/img/openmoji (scripts/fetch-openmoji.mjs). `audio` stays false until English recordings exist (scripts/generate-wortfallen-audio.mjs). British English, A1–B1; idioms-mistakes run (2026-10-30), not yet reviewed. The meanings, reactions and tips are also in public/i18n/en.json (wortfallen.<id>.*), which the build renders over the HTML: change both.

words.meaning: a farm bird; also its meat

groups.oops: I'm roasting a *kitchen* for dinner tonight.
groups.react: A whole kitchen? With the fridge and the sink? You must be really hungry!
groups.right: I'm roasting a *chicken* for dinner tonight.
groups.tip: One sentence for both: the chicken is in the kitchen. You can eat only one of them.

quiz.s: We had roast ___ with potatoes.
Our ___ is small, but the cooker is new.

words.meaning: a farm animal with wool (long ee)

groups.react: On a sheep? That was a slow and very woolly trip!
groups.tip: ship: short i, quick like a wave. sheep: long ee – make it as long as the sheep's baaa.

quiz.s: The ___ leaves Dover at nine o'clock.
The farmer has two hundred ___.

groups.oops: I haven't eaten all day – I'm so *angry*!
groups.react: Angry? With me? What have I done?
groups.right: I haven't eaten all day – I'm so *hungry*!
groups.tip: hungry starts with h, like hamburger. angry starts with a, like argh!

quiz.s: Let's have lunch, I'm really ___.
My boss was ___ because I was late again.

groups.oops: Every morning I *work* to the station.
groups.react: You do your job on the way there? That's very busy!
groups.right: Every morning I *walk* to the station.
groups.tip: In walk the l is silent and the sound is long, like in door: /wɔːk/. work sounds like bird: /wɜːk/.

quiz.s: It's a nice day – let's ___ to the park.
I ___ in a hospital as a nurse.

words.meaning: to change into something, to start to be

groups.react: You want to turn into a coffee? Hot and black?
groups.tip: False friend for German speakers: bekommen = get. become = werden: She became a doctor.

quiz.s: I ___ a lot of emails every day.
She wants to ___ a doctor.

words.meaning: it makes you ill or kills you

groups.react: A present in a bottle? How lovely! Can I open it?
groups.tip: False friend for German speakers: Gift = poison. In English a gift is always a present.

quiz.s: Thank you for the lovely birthday ___!
Keep the rat ___ away from children.

groups.oops: Our *actual* prices are on the website.
groups.react: And the other prices? Were they not real?
groups.right: Our *current* prices are on the website.
groups.tip: False friend: aktuell (German), actuel (French), attuale (Italian), actual (Spanish) = current. In English, actual means real: the actual price is the price you really pay.

quiz.s: The ___ timetable is valid until December.
The photos looked great, but the ___ hotel was awful.

words.meaning: in the end, after a long time

groups.oops: I'll *eventually* come to the party – I'm not sure yet.
groups.react: So you'll definitely come – just very, very late?
groups.right: *Maybe* I'll come to the party – I'm not sure yet.
groups.tip: False friend: eventuell (German), éventuellement (French), eventualmente (Spanish, Italian) = maybe. eventually = in the end.

quiz.s: We waited for an hour, but the bus ___ came.
___ it will rain later – take an umbrella.

groups.oops: Don't shout at him – he's very *sensible*.
groups.react: Sensible? Then he'll understand why you're shouting!
groups.right: Don't shout at him – he's very *sensitive*.
groups.tip: False friend: sensibel (German), sensible (French, Spanish) = sensitive. In English, sensible means practical: sensible shoes for a long walk.

quiz.s: Wear ___ shoes – we're walking ten miles.
My skin is very ___ to the sun.

words.meaning: you feel silly in front of other people
a baby is growing inside you

groups.oops: I'm *embarrassed* – the baby is due in May!
groups.react: Embarrassed? But a baby is wonderful news!
groups.right: I'm *pregnant* – the baby is due in May!
groups.tip: False friend for Spanish speakers: embarazada = pregnant. embarrassed = you go red because you feel silly.

quiz.s: I was so ___ when I fell over in the street.
My sister is ___ with twins.

words.meaning: you borrow books there, for free

groups.oops: I bought this novel at the *library*.
groups.react: You paid at the library? There you borrow books – for free!
groups.right: I bought this novel at the *bookshop*.
groups.tip: False friend: librería (Spanish), librairie (French), libreria (Italian) = bookshop. A library lends books.

quiz.s: You can borrow films from the ___ too.
The ___ in town sells second-hand books.

groups.react: Your chef? I didn't know you worked in a restaurant!
groups.tip: False friend: Chef (German), chef (French) = boss. In English, a chef cooks in a restaurant kitchen.

quiz.s: The ___ in this restaurant is from Naples.
I asked my ___ for a pay rise.

words.meaning: a phone you carry with you

groups.oops: Can I borrow your *handy*? Mine's dead.
groups.react: Your handy what? Your handy umbrella?
groups.right: Can I borrow your *mobile*? Mine's dead.
groups.tip: False friend for German speakers: das Handy = mobile (UK) or cell phone (US). In English, handy is an adjective: useful.

quiz.s: Call me on my ___ if you're late.
This little torch is very ___ when you go camping.

words.meaning: to take something and give it back later
to give something and get it back later

groups.oops: Can you *borrow* me ten pounds until Friday?
groups.react: Borrow you? From whom? You're not a library book!
groups.right: Can you *lend* me ten pounds until Friday?
groups.tip: You borrow FROM someone; someone lends TO you. The bank lends you money – you borrow money from the bank.

quiz.s: Can I ___ your pen for a minute?
Could you ___ me your car tomorrow?

groups.oops: The party was really *funny* – we danced all night.
groups.react: Funny? Did somebody tell jokes all night?
groups.right: The party was really *fun* – we danced all night.
groups.tip: fun = you enjoy it. funny = it makes you laugh. A holiday is fun; a clown is funny.

quiz.s: Skiing is great ___!
He told a really ___ joke.

words.meaning: a building where things are made

groups.oops: My dad works in a car *fabric*.
groups.react: A car made of fabric? Soft, but not very safe!
groups.right: My dad works in a car *factory*.
groups.tip: False friend: Fabrik (German), fábrica (Spanish), fabbrica (Italian) = factory. fabric = cloth, material.

quiz.s: The ___ makes 500 bikes a day.
This shirt is made of a soft ___.

words.meaning: the paper you get when you pay
it tells you how to cook something

groups.oops: Could I have the *recipe*, please? I might take the shoes back.
groups.react: The recipe? Do you want to cook the shoes?
groups.right: Could I have the *receipt*, please? I might take the shoes back.
groups.tip: receipt: the p is silent (/rɪˈsiːt/), you get it at the till. recipe has three syllables (/ˈresəpi/) and lives in the kitchen.

quiz.s: Keep the ___ in case you want to return it.
This cake ___ is from my grandmother.
